```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Load dataset
df <- read.csv("../data/Current_Year_Property_Assessments_(Parcel).csv",
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# --- 1. Fix ASSESSED_VALUE column ---
# Remove commas and convert to numeric
df$ASSESSED_VALUE <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", df$ASSESSED_VALUE))

# --- 2. Clean data ---
df_clean <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(COMM_NAME),
         !is.na(ASSESSED_VALUE),
         ASSESSED_VALUE > 0)

# --- 3. Community-level summary ---
community_stats <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(COMM_NAME) %>%
  summarise(
    n_parcels = n(),
    avg_assessed_value = mean(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_assessed_value = median(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_assessed_value = sd(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_assessed_value = IQR(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_assessed_value))

# --- 4. Top communities by highest average assessed value ---
top_avg <- community_stats %>%
  slice_max(order_by = avg_assessed_value, n = 10)

print("Top 10 Communities by Highest Average Assessed Value:")
print(top_avg)

# --- 5. Top communities by greatest dispersion ---
top_dispersion <- community_stats %>%
  slice_max(order_by = sd_assessed_value, n = 10)

print("Top 10 Communities by Highest Dispersion (SD) in Assessed Value:")
print(top_dispersion)


```

```{r}
# Load packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(readr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load and Clean Data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- read.csv("../data/Current_Year_Property_Assessments_(Parcel).csv",
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Fix assessed value (remove commas and convert to numeric)
df$ASSESSED_VALUE <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", df$ASSESSED_VALUE))

# Filter out missing or invalid values
df_clean <- df %>%
  filter(!is.na(COMM_NAME),
         !is.na(ASSESSED_VALUE),
         ASSESSED_VALUE > 0)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Compute Community-Level Statistics
# ------------------------------------------------------------

community_stats <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(COMM_NAME) %>%
  summarise(
    n_parcels = n(),
    avg_assessed_value = mean(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    median_assessed_value = median(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_assessed_value = sd(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    iqr_assessed_value = IQR(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  arrange(desc(avg_assessed_value))

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Top Communities (Tables)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

top_avg <- community_stats %>%
  slice_max(order_by = avg_assessed_value, n = 10)

top_dispersion <- community_stats %>%
  slice_max(order_by = sd_assessed_value, n = 10)

# Display nicely formatted tables
kable(top_avg, caption = "Top 10 Communities by Highest Average Assessed Value") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

kable(top_dispersion, caption = "Top 10 Communities by Greatest Dispersion (Standard Deviation)") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Visualization - Highest Average Assessed Values
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(top_avg, aes(x = reorder(COMM_NAME, avg_assessed_value),
                    y = avg_assessed_value)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Communities by Highest Average Assessed Value",
       x = "Community",
       y = "Average Assessed Value") +
  theme_minimal()

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Visualization - Highest Dispersion (SD)
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(top_dispersion, aes(x = reorder(COMM_NAME, sd_assessed_value),
                           y = sd_assessed_value)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(title = "Top 10 Communities by Greatest Dispersion in Assessed \nValue (SD)",
       x = "Community",
       y = "Standard Deviation of Assessed Value") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(plot.margin = margin(20, 20, 20, 20))


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Optional: Export results
# ------------------------------------------------------------

write.csv(community_stats,
          "community_assessment_statistics.csv",
          row.names = FALSE)

```



```{r}
# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Load Packages
# ------------------------------------------------------------
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(broom)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 1. Load & Clean Data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df <- read.csv(
  "../data/Current_Year_Property_Assessments_(Parcel).csv",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Clean numeric fields
df$ASSESSED_VALUE <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", df$ASSESSED_VALUE))
df$LAND_SIZE_SM   <- as.numeric(gsub(",", "", df$LAND_SIZE_SM))

# Basic filtering
df_clean <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(COMM_NAME),
    !is.na(ASSESSED_VALUE),
    ASSESSED_VALUE > 0
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 2. Create Community-Level Variables
# ------------------------------------------------------------

community_vars <- df_clean %>%
  group_by(COMM_NAME) %>%
  summarise(
    comm_avg_lot_size = mean(LAND_SIZE_SM, na.rm = TRUE),
    comm_median_value = median(ASSESSED_VALUE, na.rm = TRUE),
    
    # proportions of property types
    prop_residential   = mean(PROPERTY_TYPE == "RESIDENTIAL",   na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_commercial    = mean(PROPERTY_TYPE == "COMMERCIAL",    na.rm = TRUE),
    prop_institutional = mean(PROPERTY_TYPE == "INSTITUTIONAL", na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 3. Merge Community Variables Back Onto Parcel-Level Data
# ------------------------------------------------------------

df_model <- df_clean %>%
  left_join(community_vars, by = "COMM_NAME")

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 4. Identify & Remove Predictors with Zero Variance
# ------------------------------------------------------------

predictor_cols <- c("comm_avg_lot_size",
                    "comm_median_value",
                    "prop_residential",
                    "prop_commercial",
                    "prop_institutional")

zero_var_cols <- sapply(
  df_model[, predictor_cols],
  function(x) length(unique(x[!is.na(x)])) < 2
)

zero_var_cols   # will show TRUE/FALSE for each predictor

# Keep only valid predictors
valid_predictors <- names(zero_var_cols)[!zero_var_cols]

# Build formula dynamically
formula <- as.formula(
  paste("ASSESSED_VALUE ~ LAND_SIZE_SM +", 
        paste(valid_predictors, collapse = " + "))
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 5. Fit Regression Model
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model <- lm(formula, data = df_model)
summary(model)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 6. Table of Regression Coefficients
# ------------------------------------------------------------

model_table <- tidy(model) %>%
  mutate(across(estimate:p.value, ~ round(.x, 4)))

kable(model_table,
      caption = "Regression Results: Predicting Assessed Value from Parcel and Community Characteristics") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# 7. Residual Plot
# ------------------------------------------------------------

ggplot(data.frame(fitted = fitted(model), resid = resid(model)),
       aes(x = fitted, y = resid)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(title = "Residual Plot",
       x = "Fitted Values",
       y = "Residuals") +
  theme_minimal()

```
